Routing and packing are intrinsically coupled in transport problems, requiring joint planning for cost-efficient and physically realizable solutions. We extend the notion of an inexact first-order oracle from the Euclidean setting to Riemannian optimization, and conduct a convergence analysis for the Riemannian proximal gradient method equipped with this oracle, which we refer to as RPG-IO. Gradient-based inverse lithography technology~(ILT) for extreme ultraviolet~(EUV) masks is presented. item.description:
Anne Reulke, Mikaël Touati, Rachid El-Azouzi
Addressing infeasibility in non-cooperative games has become an important topic, as many problems across different applications face this issue. In this paper, we propose a new solution concept for generalized games with possibly infeasible individual constraints. A solution is defined as the limit of a sequence of generalized Nash equilibria induced by games with penalty terms relaxing the individual constraints. item.description:
Sebastian Steffen, Mark Cannon
We present a method of ensuring recursive feasibility and stability for robust nonlinear Model Predictive Control (MPC) with multi-step predictors. Although feasibility guarantees are well-established for the case of single-step models applied recursively over a finite horizon, such guarantees are missing in naive MPC formulations that use distinct multi-step models to predict the system state at different future points in time. item.title: Proximity operator characterization for abstract convex functions
item.description:
Ewa Bednarczuk, The Hung Tran
We consider proximity operator as a selector of the subgradient in the context of abstract convexity and characterize its properties in term of minimization problems. We also investigate the continuity and differentiability of proximity operator in the case of paraconvex and weakly convex functions. Supporting examples are given in each section.

Multi-resource allocation in network-congested, multi-tenant systems in which demand exceeds available capacity is challenging, as there is no straightforward way to determine how much of each resource to assign, especially when resources are interdependent. item.description:

This paper investigates transfer principles for generalized convexity of spectral functions on Euclidean Jordan algebras. A spectral function is induced by the eigenvalue map and an underlying symmetric function on a symmetric subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$. item.description:

This paper studies a singular dividend control problem for a firm with heterogeneous shareholders whose discount rates follow a given distribution. item.title: Formalization of Line Search Methods by Lean
item.description:
Yiyang Zhang, Kenneth W. Shum
This paper presents a formalization of line search methods in the Lean 4 theorem prover. Our goal is to advance machine verification of nonlinear optimization theory by translating standard textbook definitions and convergence arguments into rigorous Lean code. We tackle the challenging problem of stochastic weakly convex optimization subject to mixed (equality and inequality) expected-value constraints. item.description:
Mohammadreza Kamaldar
This paper presents a dual-algebraic framework for control barrier functions (CBFs) that guarantees deterministic execution using exclusively elementary arithmetic. We develop this deterministic approach to solve a fundamental bottleneck in safety-critical control: pointwise minima naturally compose intersecting safe sets, but generate non-smooth boundaries where standard Lie derivatives fail. item.description:

Gradient methods are widely used for large-scale optimization, yet their practical convergence performance depends critically on step-size selection. Most Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models build on a Vision-Language Model (VLM) backbone by attaching an action module and optimizing the full policy jointly. This design inherits strong visual and linguistic priors from the VLM, but leaves the action module to learn physical motion almost from scratch. On-policy self-distillation achieves strong pass@1 accuracy by using a single model as both teacher and student, with the teacher conditioned on a correct demonstration to provide dense token-level feedback. item.description:
Yu-Yang Chen, Lan-Zhe Guo
Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) demonstrate strong performance on standard visual question answering benchmarks, yet their scalability under controlled structural complexity remains poorly understood. item.description:
Tânia Carvalho, Maxime Cordy
Tabular foundation models are commonly assumed to present limited privacy concerns as they are often pre-trained on large collections of synthetic data. However, these models leverage in-context learning, where sensitive records may be provided directly at inference time as labelled context examples. item.description:
Shuyi Zhang, Yunfan Lou, Hongyang Cheng, Yichen Guo, Chuyao Fu et al.

item.description:
Ilia Kulikov, Chenxi Whitehouse, Tianhao Wu, Yixin Nie, Swarnadeep Saha et al.
We introduce Autodata, a general method that enables AI agents to act as data scientists who build high quality training and evaluation data.
